title: The peace prayer, honestly
hookLine: the prayer that asks to be made an instrument of peace wasn't written by Francis, though it's Franciscan in spirit

lines: ON THE FRIDGE, AT THE WEDDING.
cards: It's on the fridge magnet. It's on the framed print in the parish hall, under a friar with a bird on his hand. It's read at weddings and funerals and sung at school Masses.

It begins by asking God to make the one who prays an instrument of peace, and it often carries a name at the bottom: Saint Francis. Here's the honest part, and it's the whole lesson. Francis didn't write it.
So why does it carry his name, and does that change what it's worth?

teach.h: AN INSTRUMENT OF PEACE, IN PAIRS.
teach.b: Way back on day seventeen, you met the prayer that bears his name; today, its real story.

First, the prayer. It asks to be made an instrument of peace. Then it walks through pairs: where there is hatred, let me bring love; injury, pardon; doubt, faith; despair, hope; darkness, light; sadness, joy.
Then it turns around, asking to seek less to be comforted than to comfort, to be understood than to understand, to be loved than to love.
It ends with reversals: in giving we receive, in pardoning we are pardoned, in dying we are born to eternal life. Now the history, as historians trace it.
The prayer turns up long after Francis, in French, in a small church magazine, with no author's name. Later it was printed on a card with a picture of Francis, and the name traveled with the picture.

teach.h: A PRAYER THAT FOUND A FACE.
teach.b: No one seems to have meant to deceive; a prayer just found a face. A fake?

teach.h: NOT HIS WORDS, BUT HIS SHAPE.
teach.b: Not quite. It isn't by Francis, but it's shaped like him. In his Testament, Francis says God showed him a greeting: the Lord give you peace.
He walked into a war camp to meet a sultan. And the prayer's reversals sound like the man who said bitter became sweet.
Jesus says it in the Beatitudes, in the Douay-Rheims: "Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God." So pray it with both hands open: not his words, but his shape.

how: Catholics and other Christians pray the peace prayer at home, in schools, and at weddings, funerals and public gatherings; Franciscans greet one another with words of peace drawn from Francis's Testament.

o: the sign of peace shared during the Catholic Mass
a prayer Francis wrote on his deathbed in Assisi
a prayer for peace in Francis's spirit, not by him

games.q: the prayer's pairs — tap the pairs.

s: Saint Francis wrote the peace prayer
it turns up long after him, in French, with no author's name. it found his name through a picture.
in his Testament, Francis says God showed him a greeting of peace
the Lord give you peace: that's Francis's own.
the prayer ends with reversals: giving to receive, dying to live
in giving we receive, in pardoning we are pardoned, in dying we are born to eternal life.

games.q: you learn that a prayer you love, signed with a saint's name, wasn't written by that saint. what do you do?
o: stop praying it: it's a fake.
pray it anyway, knowing whose shape it carries.
keep telling people the saint wrote it.
games.why: it's unsigned and Francis-shaped, not his words, so the honest way is to pray it knowing both.

practice: If you know the peace prayer, pray it slowly, knowing it comes from an unnamed hand and not from Assisi.

If you don't, take one pair: bring to mind one place in your life where there is hatred, injury or sadness, hold it for a few breaths, and set beside it the word the prayer pairs with it, love, pardon or joy; if you pray, offer that pair to God, and if not, let the two words sit side by side.

wordCard.voice: The peace prayer. A prayer to be made an instrument of peace, not written by Francis, but carrying his shape and his greeting. Today's word.

orig.note: Latin: peace, the word at the heart of Francis's greeting and of the prayer that borrowed his name.

carryVoice: Your line: francis-shaped. That closes a week of lines: christ first, seven joys, the custody, the hooded friars, brother earth, and this one. Until tomorrow.
